hints: Focus on how Br and I compare in Group 17, especially atomic size and electronegativity going down the group.
Remember Br is smaller than I, so the H-Br overlap is closer and stronger, which tells you about both length and energy.
Compare the electronegativity gap for H with Br versus H with I to decide polarity, then check which statements all fit together.
walkthrough:
**Recall the Group 17 trend**

Think of Br sitting above I in Group 17. Going down, atoms get larger and less electronegative. So Br is smaller and more electronegative than I.

**Check statement 1 - bond energy**

Bond energy depends on orbital overlap. Smaller atoms overlap better and make stronger, shorter bonds.

Trend: $\text{HF} > \text{HCl} > \text{HBr} > \text{HI}$

So H-Br is stronger than H-I. Statement 1 with energy greater is correct.

**Check statement 2 - bond length**

Bond length follows atomic radius. Br has a smaller covalent radius than I, so the nuclei can sit closer together.

$$\text{bond length H-Br} < \text{bond length H-I}$$

So length less is correct.

**Check statement 3 - bond polarity**

Polarity depends on electronegativity difference, $\Delta \chi$.

$$\Delta \chi = \chi(\text{halogen}) - \chi(\text{H})$$

With $\chi(\text{H}) \approx 2.20$, $\chi(\text{Br}) \approx 2.96$, $\chi(\text{I}) \approx 2.66$, the gap is larger for HBr. So HBr is more polar. Statement 3 with polarity greater is correct.

**Combine the conclusion**

Since 1, 2 and 3 are all true, the pair that includes all three is the correct choice.

options.A: Correct because all three statements are true. HBr has greater bond energy due to better overlap, shorter bond length due to smaller Br, and greater polarity due to larger electronegativity difference than HI.
options.B: Incorrect because it leaves out statement 3. Many students correctly spot energy and length but doubt polarity. HBr is indeed more polar as Br is more electronegative than I.
options.C: Incorrect because it leaves out statement 1. Some students think larger I gives stronger bond, but bond strength decreases down the group due to poorer, more diffuse overlap, so HBr has the greater energy.
options.D: Incorrect because it includes only statement 1. This misses two other valid trends. Both bond length and polarity also follow predictable Group 17 trends that favour HBr.
